about.heading: About {app}
about.libraries_hint: Linked into the app; each keeps its own license.
backup.checksum_required: none beside it; restore needs it
backup.create_hint: Read the whole NAND twice, check that both reads match, and save the image with its SHA-256
backup.delete_description: {name} and its .sha256 are removed from the folder. This cannot be undone.
backup.delete_hint: Delete this backup and its checksum after confirmation
backup.description: Each backup is the whole NAND, with its SHA-256 beside it. A restore writes a verified image back.
backup.empty_hint: Back up unit reads the whole NAND into this folder. Do it before the first patch.
backup.restore_disabled_checksum: A SHA-256 file is required beside this backup before it can be restored
backup.restore_file_hint: Choose a NAND image to verify and restore; its SHA-256 file must be beside it
backup.restore_hint: Verify this backup and overwrite the connected thermostat's NAND after confirmation
backup.title: NAND backups
boot.description: Boots the application firmware from whatever mode the unit is in, through recovery U-Boot and the stock U-Boot from NAND.
command.connected_device: The unit on USB is a {device}.
command.disabled: Connect one 3rd generation thermostat, finish any operation, close file pickers, and disconnect any open console first
console.description: A terminal on the root shell of a patched unit, over its USB serial port. While it is open no run can start.
download.connect: Connect the USB port on the back of the display to this computer with a data cable.
download.hold_button: Hold the front panel button for 10 seconds to enter USB download mode.
download.title: Enter USB download mode
logs.delete_description: Runs older than 30 days are removed from the logs folder. The others stay.
logs.delete_old_hint: Remove run folders older than 30 days after confirmation; keep recent logs and the active run
logs.description: Every run that touches the unit keeps a log of its steps and every exchange — what an issue needs.
logs.filter_hint: Show only log lines containing this text, ignoring case
logs.reveal_hint: Open the folder containing this run's log files
nand.volume_order_hint: UBI volumes in order; hover for chip offset
nav.about_page_hint: View the app version, licenses, and credits
nav.backups_hint: Save, inspect, restore, and delete whole-NAND backups
nav.boot_hint: Boot the connected thermostat's application firmware
nav.logs_hint: Inspect the steps and logs of current and past runs
nav.patch_hint: Choose the connected thermostat's features and patch it
nav.terminal_hint: Open a USB serial root shell on a patched thermostat
nav.uboot_hint: Load recovery U-Boot and open its USB console
patch.backplate_sim_hint: nlclient drives a simulated backplate (1H1C) with a simulated temperature
patch.unsigned_updates_hint: The unit installs updates that unfr0zen's release key does not sign, such as your own builds. Off, it installs only official releases
patch.device_hint: Override the detected thermostat generation; leave on auto for USB detection
patch.device_name_hint: The thermostat's name in Home Assistant and Matter controllers, e.g. Nest FamRm; <serial> stands for its serial
patch.device_name_invalid: Device name: one line of at most 32 characters
patch.external_temperature_needs_integra: Turn on MQTT, Matter or Zigbee first: the external temperature is sent through one of them. On a 3rd generation, Bluetooth is turned off.
Turn on MQTT, Matter or Zigbee first: the external temperature is sent through one of them. The thermostat's own Bluetooth is turned off.
Turn on MQTT, Matter or Zigbee first: the external temperature is sent through one of them.
patch.external_temperature_unsupported_h: Not available on this thermostat: only the Nest Learning Thermostat regulates from an external temperature
patch.external_temperature_hint: 1st and 2nd generation: regulates from temperatures sent over MQTT, Zigbee or Matter, and goes back to its own sensor when they stop. Needs Nest firmware 5.9.4-5
patch.external_temperature_any_hint: Regulates from temperatures sent over MQTT, Zigbee or Matter, and goes back to its own sensor when they stop. 1st and 2nd generation: needs Nest firmware 5.9.4-5. 3rd generation: the thermostat's own Bluetooth is turned off, so Nest Temperature Sensors stop working
patch.external_temperature_ble_hint: 3rd generation: regulates from temperatures sent over MQTT, Zigbee or Matter, and goes back to its own sensor when they stop. The thermostat's own Bluetooth is turned off, so Nest Temperature Sensors stop working
patch.dark_theme_hint: 2nd generation: shows the settings screens in the 3rd generation's dark colours, and the boot logo on black. Needs Nest firmware 5.9.4-5
patch.entry_point_choice_hint: Choose how to enter the 3rd generation's boot ROM; auto tries all entry points
patch.entry_point_disabled_hint: Entry point selection is only available for a 3rd generation thermostat
patch.file.choose_hint: Choose a {kind} file from your computer
patch.file.clear_hint: Remove this file from the patch options; the file itself is kept
patch.matter.pairing_code_hint: The pairing code to enter in your Matter controller when adding the thermostat
patch.matter.thread_disabled_hint: Turn off Zigbee first: Thread and Zigbee cannot share the radio
patch.matter.thread_hint: Use the onboard radio for Matter over Thread; cannot be combined with Zigbee
patch.mqtt.broker_invalid: A host name or IPv4 address, optionally followed by :port (1-65535)
patch.mqtt.broker_hint: MQTT broker hostname or IP address, optionally followed by :port
patch.mqtt.ha_entity_ids: Example (non exhaustive) resulting entities in Home Assistant:
patch.mqtt.ha_entity_root_invalid: Entity ID root: lowercase letters, digits and <serial>, words joined by single _, at most 64 characters
patch.mqtt.ha_entity_root_hint: Replaces nestlocal_<serial> in every entity ID: lowercase letters and digits, words joined by _; <serial> stands for the thermostat's serial
patch.mqtt.ha_keep_about: Left empty, the thermostat keeps the names it has: Nest Thermostat and nestlocal_<serial> until it is named.
patch.mqtt.ha_move_about: Home Assistant moves the entities to these IDs with their history and settings; automations and dashboards need the new IDs.
patch.mqtt.tls_hint: Encrypt the MQTT connection with TLS; choose a CA certificate if your broker needs a private CA
patch.ntp_hint: Use your chosen NTP server to keep the thermostat's clock in sync
patch.root_password_hint: Set the root login password; leave blank to use unfr0zen
patch.start_disabled: Finish the current operation, close any file picker, and disconnect any open console before starting a run
patch.start_hint: Patch the connected thermostat with the selected options
patch.wwn_boiler_hint: With Zigbee or Thread on a Heat Link model: heat through W1 as a Works With Nest boiler. Without it, some firmware can stop on error H71/H74 with no Heat Link
patch.zigbee_disabled_hint: Turn off Thread support first: Zigbee and Thread cannot share the radio
run.disabled_busy: Finish the current operation, close any file picker, and disconnect any open console first
setup.fix_fields: Correct the fields marked in red, or turn their integration off, to continue.
terminal.clear_hint: Clear the displayed terminal output without disconnecting or sending a command
terminal.connect_disabled_hint: Select an available port and finish any other operation or console connection first
terminal.connect_hint: Open the selected USB serial port; what you type in the terminal goes to the thermostat
terminal.disconnect_hint: Close the serial connection so another operation can use USB
terminal.empty: Connect to a port. What you type goes to the unit.
terminal.port_hint: Choose the thermostat's USB serial port
uboot.description: Loads recovery U-Boot over USB and leaves it at its prompt, which keeps the watchdog serviced. Its console opens below once it is up.
update.restart_description: Restart unfr0zen to use the new version.
setup.backup_no_about: Only if you already have one.
setup.backup_note: Your backup is saved as {name}. Restore it from Backups to put the thermostat back exactly as it was.
setup.backup_yes_about: Saves the whole NAND, then patches, with the thermostat in recovery once for both. You can always restore your thermostat exactly as it is now.
setup.block_cloud_about: The thermostat only talks to your own network. It still needs Wi-Fi, but not the internet.
setup.connect_1: Take the display off its base
setup.connect_1_about: Pull it straight off. Your heating stays off until you put it back.
setup.connect_2_about: Use the micro-USB port on the back of the display and a cable that carries data. Charging-only cables are the usual problem.
setup.connect_3: Keep it connected for the whole process
setup.connect_3_about: Leave the cable in until unfr0zen says it's done. The thermostat restarts a few times along the way, and unfr0zen tells you if it needs anything from you.
setup.connect_about: unfr0zen keeps Nest's own thermostat software and adds local control. Nothing is written until you review your choices.
setup.done_about: Patched. Unplug it and put it back on its base.
setup.doom_about: The original shareware Doom, launched from the UNFR0ZEN screen.
setup.failed_about: unfr0zen stopped before finishing. The log says what happened; a backup in Backups puts the thermostat back as it was.
setup.features_about: Everything here is optional. Run the patch again any time to change it.
setup.integrations_about: Connect the thermostat to your smart home. All optional: skip this step to keep it as it is.
setup.keep_plugged_in: Keep the thermostat plugged in until it finishes
setup.matter_about: Pair with Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa or Home Assistant. Basic thermostat control. On a 3rd generation, Matter takes over the thermostat's Bluetooth, so Nest Temperature Sensors stop working.
setup.mqtt_about: Publishes the thermostat's state and takes commands through your broker. Home Assistant finds it by itself.
setup.mqtt_needs_broker: Enter your broker's address, or turn MQTT off, to continue.
setup.next_ha_about: Within a minute of joining Wi-Fi, the thermostat publishes to it; Home Assistant lists it under Settings › Devices.
setup.next_matter_about: Add a Matter device in your controller's app and enter the pairing code {code}.
setup.next_mount: Put it back on its base
setup.next_mount_about: Unplug it and push it back on. It starts as usual, on your schedule.
setup.next_zigbee_about: Permit joining in Zigbee2MQTT or ZHA; the thermostat joins as a thermostat and router.
setup.review_about: Check your choices. Patching takes a few minutes, plus the backup if you make one.
setup.running_about: Keep it plugged in. You can leave this page.
setup.ssh_about: Log in to the thermostat over Wi-Fi as root.
setup.unsupported_unit: unfr0zen supports the Nest Learning Thermostat (1st, 2nd and 3rd generation), and won't do anything to this one.
setup.usb_console_about: A root shell over the USB cable, for the Serial console page.
setup.zigbee_about: Join a Zigbee network (Zigbee2MQTT or ZHA) as a thermostat and router. Can't be combined with Thread.
setup.connect_hint: Not detected? Check the cable and the port, then wait a few seconds.
setup.done_about_backup: Backed up and patched. Unplug it and put it back on its base.
setup.integrations_skip_hint: None chosen: the thermostat keeps working on its own.
setup.developer_hint: The command line's other options, for development and testing
setup.ssh_password_login_hint: Off, only your key logs in and root's password is refused over SSH
setup.ssh_default_password_warning: With no password set, it stays unfr0zen's public default, unfr0zen: anyone on your network could log in. Set your own, or turn password login off.
setup.ssh_key_explain: A pair of files that lets this computer log in without a password. The public half goes onto the thermostat. The private half stays on this computer, and you never share it. It's safer than a password because nothing can be guessed.
setup.ssh_create_where: Saves it as ~/.ssh/unfr0zen, and picks it above
setup.ssh_login: Log in afterwards from a terminal with:
setup.ssh_needs_secret: Choose a key, or allow password login, to continue.
setup.radio_warning: Uses the thermostat's own radio: a Nest Heat Link can no longer connect to it.
